Federated Satellite Constellation Model

Interactive ModelLEO SatelliteGovernmentSovereignty

⚠ Concept model: figures are illustrative

A reference architecture in which several nations each own and contribute satellites to one shared multi-orbit constellation, run it through regional operations centres, and keep sovereign control over their assets, keys and data. Partners, satellite counts, orbits and shares are illustrative; the real-world anchors it borrows from (IRIS², Galileo, NATO NSS6G, WGS, ITU, GDPR, ITAR) are described as they actually work.

  • 8 example partner nations
  • 173 example satellites
  • 5 orbital shells (LEO to GEO)
  • 4 regional ops centres + 1 federation centre

About this model

Each partner builds, owns, files and insures its own satellites, then commits capacity to a common pool under one charter. The federation coordinates; it never owns or commands a national satellite.

The model sets out the sovereignty elements (national control of owned assets, data residency and key custody, tiered data sharing, crisis priority and pre-emption, export control, spectrum and landing rights, and governance and voting), a layered architecture and the main trade-offs and risks.

What you can explore

  • Constellation explorer: an animated ground map and orbital-shell view (300× real time), with ops centres, the follow-the-sun handover ring and failover pairs; hover any satellite, station or centre, or focus one nation.
  • Contributing nations table, sortable by capacity share, satellites or region, with capacity-share and satellites-by-nation charts.
  • Regional operations: the four regional ops centres, the Federation Coordination Center and its hot standby, and the handover and failover steps.
  • Sovereignty elements: tiered access (T0 to T3), crisis priority levels (L0 to L3), and an example voting-weight formula and chart.
  • Interactive layered-architecture diagram, filterable by national, shared-and-gated or federated control.
